project.name: Retail Point of Sale
project.purpose: Define accurate, resilient, understandable, and auditable clerk-operated checkout behavior.

payload.scope: Clerk-operated store checkout from active transaction through merchandise, tender, and completion.

authority: Add ordinary merchandise to an active transaction
Approve or cancel selected customer-facing interactions

goals: Capture and emit physical token observations
responsibilities: Associate each signal with a device delivery identity
constraints: Signals can be duplicated, malformed, delayed, or lost

authority: Act as configured product and price authority

payload.statement: The intended product, quantity, and applicable store price are represented exactly once in the active transaction.
successSignals: The applicable store price and updated total are visible
No duplicate mutation occurs for one attempt
harmSignals: Wrong product, price, quantity, or duplicate line

payload.ability: Accept merchandise input and produce an accurate or actionable transaction result.

payload.start: An authorized clerk operates an active transaction that is ready for merchandise input.
payload.end: The attempted input has a semantic result and the clerk can continue, recover, override, or cancel.

startingFacts: Store 104 Register 7 has an active authorized clerk session
Transaction T-9001 is active at revision 12
Token 012345678905 resolves to a sellable product at USD 3.49
payload.trigger: Associated scanner emits token 012345678905 with a unique delivery identity.
payload.expectedOutcome: One unit is added at USD 3.49, the total is recalculated, and the clerk sees the updated transaction.

payload.responsibility: Capture, limit, normalize transport representation, and preserve delivery identity.

payload.intent: Submit a captured token for classification.
payload.input: Device identity, delivery identity, capture time, and raw token.
payload.authority: Scanner is associated with the active register.
payload.observation: The POS workflow accepts the token or shows device guidance.

payload.responsibility: Determine the token handling category without mutating the transaction.

payload.intent: Classify the normalized token under one policy version.
payload.observation: The application routes the attempt by classification.

payload.responsibility: Resolve product identity, sellability, applicable store price, and provenance.

payload.intent: Resolve a product and applicable price for the transaction store and business instant.
payload.input: Store context, product code, business instant, and channel.
payload.observation: Owned product-price resolution result with provenance.

payload.responsibility: Evaluate sale eligibility and atomically add one priced line against the expected transaction revision.

payload.intent: Attempt to add one unit of a resolved priced product.
payload.input: Transaction, expected revision, product, store price, policy, actor authority, and attempt identity.
payload.observation: Committed transaction observation or non-mutating semantic result.

payload.responsibility: Render the accepted result or actionable path without implying uncommitted success.

payload.intent: Present the semantic result and current transaction observation.
payload.authority: Clerk can see the active transaction.
payload.observation: Updated line, quantity, price, total, status, and allowed next actions.

accessibilityConstraints: Essential actions have a keyboard path
Ordinary scanner input does not steal focus
Semantic result changes are announced appropriately

payload.statement: Reserved control, payment, and coupon patterns are evaluated according to the active classification precedence before general product-code recognition.
A product line uses the price applicable to the transaction store, channel, business instant, product, and active policy context.
Every committed transaction total equals its policy-defined composition of line extensions, taxes, fees, deposits, discounts, and adjustments in one currency.
payload.falsifyingExample: A committed line is added at USD 3.49 but the total remains USD 0.00.

payload.statement: Invalid, unknown, denied, unavailable, cancelled, duplicate, or conflicting attempts do not partially mutate the transaction.
payload.falsifyingExample: A timed-out price lookup adds a line without a price.

payload.condition: The product-price authority has no product for the classified code.
The price authority cannot return an approved result before timeout.
payload.stateEffect: The transaction remains unchanged unless an approved fallback path is modeled.

payload.description: Physical and protocol boundary between scanner and checkout application.
Boundary between store checkout responsibility and corporate product/price authority.

elements.name: Product and Store Price Resolution Contract

payload.compatibilityPolicy: A versioned owned contract maps provider details to semantic resolution results.

payload.message: Implementation Ready requires a decision among synchronous lookup, local replication, or a hybrid price-authority strategy.

claims.statement: A known sellable product scan produces exactly one correctly priced transaction line and a truthful clerk observation.
Every non-success scan result leaves the transaction unchanged by that attempt.

evidence.summary: Planned evidence set combines domain example, application integration, provider contract, PostgreSQL transaction, and browser/device scenario.
limitations: No target implementation exists in the documentation-only repository.

evidence.summary: Generate non-success outcomes and prove semantic transaction state is unchanged.
